skill.name: repo-docs
skill.description: Generates and updates README, API, architecture, contributing, and integration documentation from repository structure and dependency context.
skill.summary: Create repository documentation with integration and dependency context.
skill.author: AstraBit-CPT

content.value_statement: Repository documentation often becomes stale when dependencies, APIs, and setup steps change. This skill analyzes structure and integrations, then helps create README, API, architecture, contributing, and integration docs.
actual_capabilities: Creates README structures with quick start, usage, related repositories, and license sections.
Drafts API documentation with authentication, endpoints, request details, responses, errors, and rate limits.
Builds architecture documents that describe components, data flow, design decisions, and security notes.
Maps cross-repository dependencies, upstream services, downstream consumers, external services, and communication protocols.
Uses helper scripts to summarize repository languages, frameworks, directories, CI systems, and integration patterns.
limitations: It depends on local repository access and cannot verify private remote systems without available files.
Generated commands and links still need human validation before publishing.
Integration discovery uses pattern matching, so unusual architecture may need manual review.
It does not replace product, security, or legal review for public documentation.

use_cases.title: Prepare New Project Docs
use_cases.description: Create a complete documentation set before sharing a new repository with internal or external contributors.

use_cases.title: Refresh Stale Documentation
use_cases.description: Compare existing docs with the current codebase and update missing setup, usage, and dependency details.

use_cases.title: Map Service Dependencies
use_cases.description: Document upstream services, downstream consumers, external APIs, and communication protocols across a service ecosystem.

prompt_templates.title: Create a README
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository and draft a README with purpose, prerequisites, setup, usage, related repositories, and license sections.

prompt_templates.title: Update Existing Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current documentation against the repository files. Identify stale sections and update the README and contributing guide.

prompt_templates.title: Document APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: Create API documentation for public endpoints and functions. Include authentication, parameters, responses, errors, rate limits, and integration notes.

prompt_templates.title: Map Integrations
prompt_templates.prompt: Find cross-repository integration points and create architecture and integrations documentation with upstream, downstream, and external service relationships.

output_examples.input: Create a README for this service.
output_examples.output: A README draft with project purpose, setup prerequisites, quick start, usage, related repositories, and links to deeper docs.

output_examples.input: Document how this repository connects to other services.
output_examples.output: An integrations document listing upstream dependencies, downstream consumers, sibling repositories, external services, and communication protocols.
An architecture update with system overview, components, data flow, design decisions, scaling considerations, and security notes.

best_practices: Run the analysis from the repository root so file discovery is complete.
Review generated setup commands, repository names, and links before publishing.
Keep integration sections specific about owners, protocols, data flow, and failure handling.
anti_patterns: Publishing generated documentation without checking commands, paths, and repository names.
Omitting upstream or downstream dependencies because they live outside the current repository.
Using generic placeholders in final docs instead of real services, owners, and version constraints.

faq.question: Does this skill modify code?
faq.answer: It focuses on documentation files. It may suggest edits, but code changes are not its goal.

faq.question: Can it document private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, when the repository files are available in the local workspace for analysis.

faq.question: Does it call external services?
faq.answer: The skill guidance and bundled scripts analyze local files. Review generated links and commands before use.

faq.question: What documents can it create?
faq.answer: It supports README, API, architecture, contributing, and integration documentation.

faq.question: How accurate is integration discovery?
faq.answer: It uses repository structure and pattern matching, so final results need maintainer review.

faq.question: Does it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. Maintainers should verify commands, service names, security details, and ownership information.
